methods: For the spatial-support diagnostic, all 25 grid-cell series and their equal-weight regional mean use the same 18,404 training prediction-target times. We first form the regional mean at each time and then take its empirical 95th percentile, rather than averaging grid-cell quantiles. This gives Q95 $=0.574048$~mm\,h$^{-1}$ on the original precipitation scale, without a logarithmic transformation. Individual-cell Q95 values range from 0.5441 to 0.6990~mm\,h$^{-1}$. Q95 defines a fixed relative upper-tail regime of the regional hourly target, not a meteorological heavy-rainfall category.
results: A separate descriptive spatial comparison uses the training targets, rather than the forecast-test samples. Relative to the median of the corresponding statistic across the 25 cells, regional wet-hour frequency ($\geq0.1$~mm\,h$^{-1}$) is 14.3\% higher and Q90 is 8.8\% higher. Regional Q95 is 7.3\% lower than the cell median but remains within the individual-cell range. Regional Q99, Q99.9 and the maximum are lower by 13.1\%, 13.9\% and 31.4\%, respectively, and all three are below the corresponding values of every one of the 25 cells. These percentages are relative changes, not percentage-point differences.
support: Supplementary Table~\ref{supp-stab:r2m7_spatial_quantiles} lists the 26 series on the common training-time set. Supplementary Figure~\ref{supp-sfig:r2m7_spatial_quantiles} divides each displayed statistic by the median of that same statistic across the 25 cells. Its five categories therefore have separate normalizing denominators, with a reference ratio of one.
discussion: The spatial contrasts depend on the position in the precipitation distribution: wet frequency and Q90 increase relative to the cell medians, while the higher quantiles and maxima decrease. Spatial averaging should therefore not be described as reducing every precipitation intensity. These are descriptive contrasts between matched-time series summaries; the individual maxima need not occur at the same time, and the comparison does not identify an event-scale causal mechanism.
limitations: On the common training-target set, the regional Q99, Q99.9 and maximum are 13.1\%, 13.9\% and 31.4\% below their respective 25-cell medians. The opposite-direction contrasts in wet frequency and Q90 qualify a blanket smoothing interpretation. A single ERA5 cell is itself a gridded estimate rather than a rain-gauge measurement, so these grid-to-region comparisons do not quantify station-level extreme-rainfall attenuation. The conclusions concern ERA5-derived regional-mean hourly precipitation and do not directly represent station-scale extremes.
